subject: Geo ownership and replication policy discussion
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@medisyshealth.com>, Medisys Security <security@medisyshealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Geo ownership and replication policy discussion

Hi Elena (+security team),

Thanks again for the chat earlier — appreciate the clear questions from your ops & security folks. Per our call, I wanted to summarize the scenarios we discussed and capture a few concrete asks so we can confirm feasibility and timelines. Attaching the quick matrix I referenced.

Key points from the call:
- Primary requirement: customer data for EU and US tenants must be "owned" in-region for serving and logs, with cross-region copies only for DR under strict controls.
- Acceptable DR model: asynchronous encrypted replication to a secondary region (warm standby) with explicit customer approval for failover.
- Backups: periodic encrypted snapshots retained per your retention policy (we discussed 90 days for operational logs, 365 days for audit artifacts; happy to adjust).
- PII handling: Redwood supports field-level redaction and a PII tagging flag in ingestion; we can optionally minimize token logging for flagged flows.
- Logging: access logs, audit trails, and request/response traces can be retained in-region; we also offer field-level obfuscation and token-sampling to reduce exposure.

Open items / asks for your team:
1) Can security confirm whether cross-region encrypted backups (at-rest) are permissible for your DR policy if the replicas are configured as immutable and access is via customer KMS?
2) What RPO/RTO targets should we design for the warm-standby region? We proposed RPO=1h / RTO=2h in the call as a baseline.
3) Any constraints on third-party-managed keys vs. customer-managed KMS/HSM? (We can support either; customer-managed KMS is preferred for stricter controls.)

Next steps I propose:
- I will share the matrix & post-call notes (attached).
- If helpful, Marissa can run a short technical review and propose a minimal canary plan for failover testing.
- We can schedule a short follow-up with your security engineer to walk through KMS/replication configuration and the immutable snapshot approach.

Attachments: postcall-notes-20260921.pdf, region-replication-matrix-20260921.xlsx

Best,
Markus Klein
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Date: Tue, 21 Sep 2026 16:18:00 -05:00
Subject: Re: Geo ownership and replication policy discussion

Markus —

Thanks for the summary and the matrix — that helps. A few clarifying questions from our security team: 

1) When you say "immutable snapshots," do those live in the same region as the primary by default, or can they be routed to a dedicated archival region under customer control? We need to ensure retention enforcement cannot be bypassed.
2) For PII tagging/redaction, can that be applied at ingestion only (so upstream systems never persist PII), or is it post-processing? Our preference is upstream redaction.
3) Regarding logs: can you provide an example of the access control model for audit logs (RBAC groups, time-limited access tokens, and audit trail exports)?

Also looping in our security lead, Sam Patel (sam.patel@medisyshealth.com), who will own the deeper review. He may request evidence (SOC 2 artifact, encryption architecture diagram).

Elena
Dir. Product Ops, Medisys Health
[Attachment: security-questions-annotated.pdf]

From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@medisyshealth.com>, Medisys Security <security@medisyshealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 22 Sep 2026 09:34:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Geo ownership and replication policy discussion

Hi Elena / Sam —

Answers inline to keep things tidy: 

1) Immutable snapshots: by default our snapshot lifecycle keeps the primary copy in-region. For DR we can replicate snapshots to a customer-designated archival region, but that copy is created only if the customer enables cross-region replication and links a customer-managed KMS. The replication workflow is auditable (we write events to the in-region audit log before replication).

2) PII tagging/redaction: we support both models. Ingestion-time tagging + redaction is available (recommended) — that prevents sensitive fields from ever being written to long-term logs. Post-processing redaction is possible but is treated as a higher-risk workflow and we log the operation. We included configuration examples in the attached matrix.

3) Audit logs access model: RBAC with scope-limited roles (read-only-audit, admin, escalation). Time-limited access tokens are issued via our portal and recorded in an immutable audit trail. Exports are available as encrypted bundles; we can configure an automated export to your SFTP or to a customer-owned GCS/Azure bucket with KMS key wrap.

Evidence: attaching our SOC2 summary & the encryption architecture diagram link. If Sam wants full artifacts we can schedule a secure transfer (we typically deliver under an NDA or via an ephemeral share).

Proposed short next steps:
- Marissa to propose a 2-week canary plan (minimal traffic failover test + sampling verification).
- Security to confirm whether cross-region immutable backup is acceptable under customer-managed KMS (answer needed to size replication windows).
- If accepted, Redwood can provide an estimated timeline: 3-4 weeks to enable replication + 1 week for canary test scheduling.

Attachments: SOC2-summary-20260922.pdf
Links: https://drive.google.com/file/d/encryption-architecture-diagram

Thanks,
Markus

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Subject: Fwd: Geo ownership and replication policy discussion

Markus / Priya —

Forwarding the thread so I can draft the canary plan. Quick notes:
- Canary should exercise: 1) in-region serving with PII-tagged payloads, 2) failover to warm standby (read-only) and validate that immutable snapshots replicate, 3) replay audit log export to customer bucket.
- Minimal traffic: 50–200 synthetic transactions over 1 hour, include a mix of 4 prompting templates we use in the ops playbook.
- Required from Medisys: confirmation of KMS type, the archival region (if allowed), and contact for runbook sign-off.

I'll aim to share a draft plan by EOD tomorrow with runbook steps, test phasing, and rollback criteria.

-Marissa
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference
